rules.statement: Enforce authorization checks on all authenticated endpoints. Ensure a user cannot access or modify resources belonging to another user (IDOR prevention).

Never store passwords in plaintext or with a fast general-purpose hash (MD5, SHA-1, or bare SHA-256). Use a slow, salted, password-specific algorithm (bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2). Encrypt sensitive data in transit (TLS) and at rest.
Never interpolate user input directly into SQL queries, NoSQL queries, OS commands, or LDAP queries. Use parameterized queries or safe ORMs.

Threat-model security-critical flows (authentication, payments, access control, account recovery) before implementation, not as a retrofit. Do not rely solely on input validation to compensate for a flow that is unsafe by design — for example, a password-recovery endpoint that returns a different response depending on whether the email exists.
Do not expose detailed error messages or stack traces in production API responses.
Track the exact versions of every third-party dependency and remove unused ones. Do not knowingly ship a dependency with a publicly disclosed, unpatched CVE relevant to how it is used.
Enforce strong password policies, implement rate limiting on login endpoints to prevent brute-forcing, and invalidate session tokens on logout.

Verify the integrity of software updates, CI/CD pipeline artifacts, and critical serialized data (e.g. via digital signatures or checksums) before trusting or deploying them. Do not deserialize untrusted data without an integrity check.

Log authentication attempts, access-control failures, and input-validation failures with enough context to support incident investigation. Never log sensitive data — passwords, tokens, full card numbers, PII — in plaintext.

Validate and sanitize any user-supplied URL or hostname before the server uses it to make an outbound request. Enforce an allowlist of permitted destinations rather than a denylist, and block requests to internal/link-local address ranges.
Minimize the Tauri `allowlist` in `tauri.conf.json`. Only enable the specific API endpoints (e.g., `fs`, `shell`) required by the application.

Do not use interactive ARIA roles (e.g., `role="button"`) on non-interactive elements (like `<div>` or `<span>`) without also implementing `tabindex` and keyboard event handlers (`keydown`, `keyup`). Prefer native semantic HTML.
Run scripts directly using `bun run` instead of `npm run` to bypass the slow Node.js boot time.
Avoid deeply nested quantifiers (e.g., `(a+)+`) in Regular Expressions that are evaluated against untrusted input.
Avoid using the `shell.execute` or `shell.open` APIs with unvalidated user input to prevent command injection.

Define a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) in `tauri.conf.json` preventing external script execution and inline scripts.
Domain logic (entities, use cases) must not import or depend on infrastructure logic (database drivers, HTTP clients, UI frameworks).
Use lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum`) and commit them to version control to guarantee deterministic builds across environments.

Every environment variable the code reads must be documented in the repository (an `.env.example`, the README, a compose file, a Dockerfile or a CI workflow), so a new engineer can configure the project without reading the source.

EditorConfig "trim_trailing_whitespace" = "false" for *.md
Every repository must have a `README.md` at the root containing local setup instructions, architecture overview, and test commands.
Always use strict equality (`===` and `!==`) instead of loose equality (`==` and `!=`).
Exported module functions must have explicit return types rather than relying on inference.
Validate invariants and arguments at the boundary of a function or class. Throw an error immediately rather than proceeding with invalid state.
Do not set `outline: none` or `outline: 0` in CSS without providing a custom, high-contrast `:focus` state.
Every form input (e.g., `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`) must have an associated `<label>`. Use the `for` attribute on the label pointing to the input's `id`, or nest the input inside the label.
All `` elements must have an `alt` attribute. If the image is purely decorative, use `alt=""`.
Build artifacts (like Docker images or binaries) must be immutable. Deploy the exact same artifact to staging and production, modifying only the injected environment variables.
Always validate and sanitize data received via Tauri IPC (`invoke`) in the Rust backend. Never trust client payloads.
Restore or clear spies and mocked globals (such as `vi.spyOn`, `jest.spyOn`, `sinon.spy`, or environment overrides) in `afterEach` blocks or using `mockRestore` to prevent test state leakage.
Error messages thrown in the codebase must contain actionable information. Avoid generic errors like `Something went wrong`.
Do not execute database queries inside loops. Use batching (e.g., DataLoader) or explicit JOIN/eager-loading mechanisms.
Every test should contain at least one verifiable assertion (e.g. `expect`, `assert`, or verified thrown exception) to confirm the expected behavior.
Do not pass an `async` callback to `forEach`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises, so the work is not awaited and its errors are lost; use `for...of` or `await Promise.all(items.map(...))`.
Avoid putting complex logic or multiple side-effects inside a single `$: ` reactive statement to prevent unpredictable cascading updates.
Avoid empty test blocks or tests containing only comments. Empty tests give a false sense of test coverage without actually verifying any behavior.
Never use `eval()` or pass strings to `setTimeout`/`setInterval`. This is a severe security vulnerability.
Avoid using the `any` type. Use `unknown` if the type is truly dynamic, and apply type narrowing.
Do not add properties or methods to the prototypes of native objects like `Object`, `Array`, or `String`.
Promises must be explicitly awaited, returned, or have `.catch()` called on them.
Do not commit focused tests (such as `it.only`, `test.only`, `describe.only`, `fit`, or `fdescribe`). Focused tests silence the rest of the test suite and can hide regressions.
Never hardcode API keys, passwords, or connection strings in source code. Inject them via environment variables or a secure secret manager.
Avoid using `new Function()` with dynamic strings, as it operates identically to `eval()` and opens XSS vectors.
Avoid defining functions inside loops unless they exclusively reference block-scoped variables, otherwise loop closures will capture the final state.
Do not use magic numbers or raw strings in domain logic. Define them as explicit named constants or enums.
Prefer string enums or union types over numeric enums. If using numeric enums, always explicitly assign values.
Use `let` or `const` instead of `var` to ensure block scoping and prevent hoisting bugs.
Always implement pagination (cursor or offset) when returning collections of data from an API. Never return unbounded lists.
Use arrow functions for callbacks to preserve the lexical scope of `this`.
Use `as const` to infer the narrowest possible literal types rather than explicitly typing out literal unions.
Use `Bun.serve()` for HTTP servers instead of the Node.js `http` module. It is highly optimized and natively supports Web standard Request/Response.
Use the built-in `bun:test` module instead of `jest` or `vitest`. It is significantly faster and natively supports TypeScript/JSX.
Use the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) instead of logical OR (`||`) when providing default values for nullable variables.
Use object spread syntax (`{ ...obj }`) instead of `Object.assign()` for shallow copying and merging.
Mark properties, arrays, and tuples as `readonly` when they are not intended to be mutated.
Use template literals (`\```) for string interpolation rather than string concatenation (`+`).
Mutations to arrays or objects will not trigger Svelte reactivity unless an assignment operator (`=`) is used. E.g., `arr = [...arr, val]` instead of `arr.push(val)`.
Functions declared `async` must contain an `await` expression unless explicitly implementing an interface that requires a Promise.
Adhere to Semantic Versioning (SemVer). Do not introduce breaking changes without bumping the major version number.
Classes and modules should have exactly one reason to change. Separate data fetching from presentation.
Always use the `$` prefix (e.g., `$store`) to auto-subscribe and unsubscribe from Svelte stores inside components. Do not manually `store.subscribe` without handling `onDestroy`.
Do not use the non-null assertion operator (`!`). Handle nullability explicitly with optional chaining (`?.`) or control flow narrowing.
Avoid using `{@html content}`. If required, sanitize the `content` on the server or via a robust library like DOMPurify before rendering.
Ensure asynchronous operations inside tests are awaited or returned as Promises. Floating async operations can cause tests to complete prematurely or fail silently.
Use `Bun.file()` for I/O operations instead of `fs.readFile`. It leverages the fastest system-level I/O mechanisms (like `sendfile`).
Use `bun:sqlite` for local SQLite databases. It is a highly optimized, native driver that avoids FFI overhead.
Always provide a unique key identifier when using `{#each items as item (item.id)}` to maintain state correctly across re-renders.
